'docs/PRD.md':'''# Product requirements

## Product

greenfield-proof is a small TypeScript reusable greeting API plus CLI for developers.

## Audience

Developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI.

## Platforms

Node22+ Linux. The cached setup generator requires Node 22.12+ within the Node 22 line; the observed host is 22.23.2. Mobile: none.

## Constraints

npm; tsup with TypeScript and node:test; private UNLICENSED fixture, no publishing. No framework runtime or runtime dependency. Development tooling includes TSX and Zod for copied roadmap helpers. All npm cache and logs stay in this scratch repository. No product remote, deployment, or commit is authorized.

## Non-goals

No external service, authentication, mobile application, web UI, deployment, or publishing. The API is an imported function, not a network backend.

## Success signals

The public export greet(name?: string) returns Hello, <name>"'!, defaults to world, and rejects blank names with TypeError. Nonblank names are preserved verbatim. The CLI contract is owned by [UX canon](ux-canon.md). Meaningful API and CLI tests, typecheck, build, config validation, catalog validation, and roadmap emission must pass.

## Brand

Non-Blade. Component registry: absent/none because this is a text CLI and reusable library. No visual tokens, fonts, palette, spacing system, or UI assets are needed.

## Decisions

| Date | Ruling | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-05 | APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN received as a separate input after the complete proposal | Authorizes only the proposed scratch artifacts and ordered commands; this record is written only during approved execution |
| 2026-09-05 | library-cli; tsup + node:test; npm | Small reusable TypeScript API and thin CLI with minimal test dependencies |
| 2026-09-05 | Adapt cached create-vite 8.3.0 vanilla-ts output in the existing scratch root | User selected the verified cached public generator; avoid another repository and remove the web demo |
| 2026-09-05 | Non-UI design; registry none | No rendered UI or Blade branding |

The approved operation scope is generation, guarded adaptation of the exact files, source checker copy, one roadmap init/config adaptation, scratch-local dependency installation, and the individually proposed verification commands. The seven gate bindings live in roadmap/roadmap.config.json. Lint is absent because no linter is selected; E2E is absent because there is no separate browser/service runner. CLI process behavior remains tested.

## Unknowns

Future distribution, release cadence, support policy, localization, and any future UI or backend requirements are unknown. Do not infer them. A separate read-only brownfield re-audit remains required after execution; no idempotence claim is made.
'"''',
'docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md':'''# ADR 0001: Tech stack

## Context

A small private TypeScript greeting library and CLI for developers on Node22+ Linux. npm and tsup with node:test were explicitly selected. No network backend, web application, mobile application, or monorepo is required.

## Options: Library/CLI

Source: installed zeroh-greenfield skills/stack-decision/references/matrices.md, Library/CLI matrix. Rows preserved verbatim:

| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsup + node:test | Compact bundling with built-in tests | Two separate tools | Small TypeScript package values minimal test dependencies | Exported modules and fixtures | tsup |
| tsdown + vitest | Modern bundling and rich tests | Additional test dependency | Vite-aligned libraries need fast test ergonomics | Exported modules and test helpers | tsdown |
| unbuild | Convention-led library output | Less explicit build control | Multi-format package follows unjs conventions | Package presets and modules | unbuild |

## Ruling: 2026-09-05

Selected: tsup + node:test. Reason: the user selected a small TypeScript reusable greeting API plus CLI with minimal test dependencies. Use npm, ESM, strict TypeScript, tsup declarations, and built-in node:test.

The installed library-cli archetype selects create-vite "'^8 vanilla-ts as the generator. Use the user-verified cached create-vite 8.3.0 and adapt its my-lib destination to this existing scratch root. Remove the generated web demo and Vite dependency. Vite/create-vite and tsup are MIT, Allowed anywhere; TypeScript is Apache-2.0; Node typings, TSX, and Zod are MIT development tooling. No framework runtime is retained.

## Consequences

API and CLI stay separate source entry points. Tests run against built public exports and CLI processes, so build precedes node:test. TSX and Zod support the copied roadmap emitter as development dependencies. npm writes a lockfile; npm state stays under .npm-cache and .npm-logs. The package remains private and UNLICENSED with no publishing.

## Revisit conditions

Revisit if a second output format is required, a browser or network backend becomes a committed requirement, or tests require capabilities unavailable in node:test. Future distribution and release policy remain unknown. Non-Blade and registry-none reasons are recorded in [ADR 0002](0002-design-system.md).

'docs/adr/0002-design-system.md':'''# ADR 0002: Non-UI design

## Context and options

This product exposes an imported function and a text CLI. The installed design reference provides web/mobile mappings and a Blade handoff; none applies to the explicitly selected non-UI, non-Blade fixture. There is no applicable design-system matrix row to fabricate.

Considered applicability: text CLI contract is required; web component systems, mobile theme mappings, and Blade theme ownership are outside the supplied scope.

## Ruling: 2026-09-05

Select no visual design system. Registry: absent/none, because no UI components are consumed. Brand: non-Blade. Do not invent tokens, fonts, palette, spacing values, or branded assets. The [UX canon](../ux-canon.md) owns the text interaction contract.

## Consequences

Use plain text stdout for success and help, stderr for invalid input, and stable exit codes. No component registry, components.json, token home, or design sibling is required.

## Revisit conditions

Revisit when a rendered UI, branded visual surface, or mobile application is approved. Future visual identity and localization remain unknown.

'docs/ux-canon.md':'''# UX canon

## Visual language

Plain text CLI. Non-Blade. No visual tokens, fonts, palette, spacing system, or component registry; these do not apply to a reusable library and terminal command.

## Component vocabulary

One optional name argument, one --help option, stdout, stderr, and process exit status.

## Interaction rules

With no argument, print Hello, world"'! followed by a newline and exit 0. With one nonblank name, print Hello, <name>! followed by a newline and exit 0. Preserve nonblank names verbatim; quote names containing spaces in the shell.

With exactly --help, print the following text followed by a newline to stdout and exit 0:

    Usage: greenfield-proof [name]
           greenfield-proof --help

Unknown options, including -prefixed arguments, or more than one argument print that usage to stderr and exit 1 without stdout. Blank names print Name must not be blank followed by usage to stderr and exit 1. There are no color codes, prompts, external calls, or interactive states.

## Binding design system

None. [ADR 0002](adr/0002-design-system.md) records the non-UI choice and absent-registry reason. No token home is invented. Future localization and visual requirements are unknown.
'"''',
'AGENTS.md':'''# Repository guidance

## Conventions

Keep the pure reusable API in src/index.ts and the executable adapter in src/cli.ts. Use the configured TypeScript compiler and tsup build. Tests use node:test against built outputs. Keep one canonical documentation home per fact and link to it. Keep npm cache and logs scratch-local during this fixture.

## Don't

Do not publish, deploy, add a product remote, commit in this fixture, or invent framework, service, authentication, mobile, brand, token, or registry requirements. Do not duplicate conventions into harness files. Do not replace existing homes or generated harness blocks.

## Generalize-forward

Reuse the greeting API from the CLI. Extract further shared abstractions only when at least two concrete consumers justify the boundary; retain unknown future requirements explicitly.

## Flag-first delivery

For future optional behavior, propose the flag and default before implementation. This fixture implements only the approved baseline greeting contract and introduces no speculative flag framework.

## Release hold

hold[]: publishing, deployment, release automation, and product remote creation. Separate authorization is required. Roadmap phase planning belongs to zeroh-roadmap.

## Product

greenfield-proof is a small TypeScript reusable greeting API plus CLI for developers.

## Audience

Developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI.

## Platforms

Node22+ Linux. The cached setup generator requires Node 22.12+ within the Node 22 line; the observed host is 22.23.2. Mobile: none.

## Constraints

npm; tsup with TypeScript and node:test; private UNLICENSED fixture, no publishing. No framework runtime or runtime dependency. Development tooling includes TSX and Zod for copied roadmap helpers. All npm cache and logs stay in this scratch repository. No product remote, deployment, or commit is authorized.

## Non-goals

No external service, authentication, mobile application, web UI, deployment, or publishing. The API is an imported function, not a network backend.

## Success signals

The public export greet(name?: string) returns Hello, <name>"'!, defaults to world, and rejects blank names with TypeError. Nonblank names are preserved verbatim. The CLI contract is owned by [UX canon](ux-canon.md). Meaningful API and CLI tests, typecheck, build, config validation, catalog validation, and roadmap emission must pass.

## Brand

Non-Blade. Component registry: absent/none because this is a text CLI and reusable library. No visual tokens, fonts, palette, spacing system, or UI assets are needed.

The seven gate bindings live in roadmap/roadmap.config.json. Lint is absent because no linter is selected; E2E is absent because there is no separate browser/service runner. 'docs/ux-canon.md':'''# UX canon

## Visual language

Plain text CLI. Non-Blade. No visual tokens, fonts, palette, spacing system, or component registry; these do not apply to a reusable library and terminal command.

## Component vocabulary

One optional name argument, one --help option, stdout, stderr, and process exit status.

## Interaction rules

With no argument, print Hello, world"'! followed by a newline and exit 0. With one nonblank name, print Hello, <name>! followed by a newline and exit 0. Preserve nonblank names verbatim; quote names containing spaces in the shell.

With exactly --help, print the following text followed by a newline to stdout and exit 0:

    Usage: greenfield-proof [name]
           greenfield-proof --help

Unknown options, including -prefixed arguments, or more than one argument print that usage to stderr and exit 1 without stdout. Blank names print Name must not be blank followed by usage to stderr and exit 1. There are no color codes, prompts, external calls, or interactive states.

## Binding design system

None. [ADR 0002](adr/0002-design-system.md) records the non-UI choice and absent-registry reason. No token home is invented. Future localization and visual requirements are unknown.
